newsitem.title: USA: Aluminum beverage can recycling rate rises in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Aluminum beverage can recycling rate rises in 1996.

text.p: The recycling rate for aluminum cans in the United States rose 1.3 percent to 63.5 percent in 1996 compared to the previous year, the Aluminum Association and Institute of Scrap Recycling Industries said.
In 1996 the aluminum industry paid some $1.08 billion to recyclers for their used beverage cans.
Last year the U.S. produced 99 billion aluminum beverage cans of which 62.8 billion were returned for recycling.
The number of cans manufactured per pound of alumium rose to 31.92 because thinner sheet was used.
As a result, the 62.8 billion cans collected totals 1.97 billion pounds of metal or 893,578 tonnes, representing a decrease in aluminum recycled of 2.4 percent from 1995.
